;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]], [[Northern Syria Buffer Zone]]
**Turkish officials say that [[Turkish Air Force]] jets have begun [[Bombardment|bombing]] the [[Syrian-Iraqi border]] on Monday night, ahead of an imminent [[invasion]] of northern [[Syria]]. That region is controlled by [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish]]-led [[Syrian Democratic Forces]], whom Turkey regards as terrorists. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/464841-turkey-confirms-strikes-on-syrian-border-ahead-of-offensive-report (''The Hill'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**A bomb explodes in a classroom at [[Ghazni University]] in [[Afghanistan]], wounding at least nineteen students. The same university was targeted last month with a bomb attached to a university [[minibus]]. That bomb killed one person and injured five others. [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/afghanistan-bomb-goes-off-inside-classroom-wounds-19-1.66988845 (''Gulf News'')]
*Two [[sapper]]s die and four more are wounded trying to defuse [[World War II]] shells in Poland. The last such casualties occurred in 1982. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-10/09/c_138456810.htm (Xinhua)] [https://www.tvn24.pl/gen-boguslaw-bebenek-to-pierwszy-od-1982-r-smiertelny-wypadek-zolnierzy-podczas-rozminowania,975760,s.html (TVN24)]

;Health and environment
*[[Pacific Gas and Electric Company|Pacific Gas and Electric]] shuts off power to 800,000 customers in [[Northern California]], citing safety concerns over an elevated fire risk caused by weather conditions. [https://sacramento.cbslocal.com/2019/10/08/pge-power-shutoffs-norcal/ (CBS 13 Sacramento)] 

;International relations
*[[Brexit negotiations in 2019]]
**[[President of the European Council]] [[Donald Tusk]] tells [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]] [[Boris Johnson]] that "what's at stake is not a stupid blame game," after a UK source said that talks were "close to breaking down" following a reported argument in a phone call between Johnson and [[Chancellor of Germany|German chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] about the post-Brexit status of [[Northern Ireland]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/10/08/uk/donald-tusk-brexit-boris-johnson-gbr-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[China–United States relations]], [[China–United States trade war]]
**The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] imposes visa restrictions on numerous [[China|Chinese]] government officials whom it believes responsible for the [[Xinjiang re-education camps|detention]] or [[Human_rights_in_China#Uyghur_Muslims|abuse]] of [[Islam in China|Muslim]] [[Uighurs]] and other [[Ethnic minorities in China|ethnic minorities]] in [[Xinjiang|Xinjiang province]]. On Monday the [[United States Department of Commerce|Department of Commerce]] added twenty-eight Chinese firms and bureaus to its "trade blacklist" for similar reasons. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-china-muslims/u-s-imposes-visa-restrictions-on-chinese-officials-over-muslim-treatment-idUSKBN1WN29H (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*Thirteen men are arrested in the [[United Kingdom]] for drug smuggling. The authorities believe that over several years, the suspects imported approximately 50 tonnes of illegal drugs from the [[Netherlands]], valued at several tens of millions of [[Pound sterling|pounds]]. The [[National Crime Agency]] called it “the biggest ever [drug] conspiracy that we've seen in the UK”. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-49973186 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Ecuadorian protests]]
**The [[Government of Ecuador]], headed by President [[Lenín Moreno]], moves to [[Guayaquil]] as the [[Carondelet Palace]] in [[Quito]] is taken over by protesters and chaos persists in the capital. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/08/ecuador-moves-government-out-of-capital-as-violent-protests-rage (''The Guardian'')]
**As the situation in the country worsens, [[Lenín Moreno|Moreno]] denounces a "coup attempt" by incumbent President [[Nicolás Maduro]] of Venezuela and former Ecuadorian President [[Rafael Correa]]. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/sns-bc-lt--ecuador-political-crisis-20191008-story.html (''Chicago Tribune'')]
*[[Politics of Italy]]
**[[Italy|Italian]] lawmakers vote to reduce the number of seats in the [[Chamber of Deputies (Italy)|Chamber of Deputies]] from 630 to 400, and the number of seats in the [[Senate of the Republic (Italy)|Senate of the Republic]] from 315 to 200, at the [[next Italian general election]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-italy-politics-parliament/italian-parliament-votes-to-scrap-hundreds-of-seats-at-next-election-idUSKBN1WN1VK (Reuters)]
*[[Politics of Azerbaijan]]
**[[Prime Minister of Azerbaijan|Prime Minister]] [[Novruz Mammadov]] presents his resignation as [[President of Azerbaijan|President]] appoints [[Ali Asadov]] to the office. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/azerbaijan-pm-resigns-president-replaces-loyalist-191008092046855.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://eurasianet.org/azerbaijan-replaces-prime-minister (Eurasianet)]
;Science and technology
*The [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] is awarded to [[Jim Peebles]] for theoretical discoveries in physical cosmology, and to [[Michel Mayor]] and [[Didier Queloz]] for the discovery of [[51 Pegasi b]], an exoplanet orbiting a solar-type star. [https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-49960497 (BBC News)]
